model.title: Taxpayer Workforce Modernization Act
model.meta: Ways and Means Committee · Rep. David Schweikert (R-AZ)

summary.text: The bill would require the IRS to create a fellowship program by September 30, 2026, to recruit private-sector data scientists and other qualified tax experts, with at least 10 fellows staffed at the Commissioner's discretion and at least 5 kept filled at all times. The fellows would serve on a new IRS task force that would develop data-driven methods for selecting audits, help with offshore tax evasion and Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act issues, train IRS staff in data analytics, and review how artificial intelligence is used in tax administration. Fellows would be hired for two-, three-, or four-year terms, with unlimited one-year extensions, and the IRS could hire them permanently at the end of a term. Their pay would be set by the Treasury Secretary, but not below the minimum for the GS-15 pay scale and not above the limit set in federal law. The Commissioner would also have to report to Congress each year on the program's effects and return on investment, and recommend any changes.
